title: CERT-In issues advisory on eMudhra cybersecurity fiasco, suggests best practices for online security - India Today
body:
Published by

Ankita Garg

Oct 21, 2026 16:03 IST

India’s cybersecurity agency CERT-In has issued an advisory warning about a security compromise involving eight intermediate digital certificate authorities linked to Indian company eMudhra. The flaw could allow attackers to create fake security certificates for websites they do not control, potentially enabling them to impersonate legitimate websites or interfere with encrypted internet communications. [...] In its advisory dated October 21, CERT-In said the affected private cryptographic keys were generated with insufficient randomness, making them vulnerable to recovery. The agency has recommended security updates, checks for affected certificates and changes to certificate trust settings to reduce the risk. The incident involves TLS certificates, which play an important role in securing websites and protecting information exchanged between users and online services.

-Verify TLS certificates: Check certificate chains, issuing authorities, validity periods and revocation status. CERT-In has also advised against bypassing certificate-validation warnings or disabling certificate verification.

title: The New Oil? Why Semiconductors Are Shaping the Global Economy - Boston Trust Walden
body: One of the clearest signs that semiconductors have become strategic infrastructure is to identify who is funding them, as governments are now semiconductor investors, too. The United States, European Union, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and China have all introduced large-scale industrial policies intended to strengthen domestic semiconductor ecosystems through tax incentives, manufacturing subsidies, workforce development, research funding, and even outright equity ownership. These investments [...] Moreover, geography has become a competitive advantage. Few industries illustrate globalization more clearly. For instance, a smartphone designed in California may incorporate intellectual property developed in the United Kingdom, fabrication equipment built in the Netherlands and Japan, manufacturing in Taiwan, advanced memory from South Korea, and final assembly elsewhere in Asia. No single country controls the entire semiconductor value chain. Yet, several of its most important links remain [...] These investments are not simply about economic growth. They reflect a growing consensus that computing capability increasingly determines technological leadership, military preparedness, productivity growth, and long-term economic competitiveness. The semiconductor industry is therefore becoming one of the few industries simultaneously shaped by private capital, public policy, and geopolitical strategy. That combination is both unusual and historically significant.
